# Houston

> Houston is a free, cross-platform desktop coding agent that you point at your own AI model. Give it a project folder and it reads, edits, searches, and runs code — with every consequential action gated by an approval flow and, where the OS supports it, shell commands run in a sandbox. It runs locally and collects no analytics or telemetry.

## What it is

- Type: desktop application (macOS, Windows, Linux), built with Electron, React, and TypeScript.
- Price: free. You bring your own model API keys, or run a local model; you pay only your provider's usage, never Houston.
- Bring your own model: Claude (Anthropic), GPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and local models via Ollama or LM Studio. Switch models per conversation.
- Privacy: runs on your device; no telemetry. Data leaves only to providers you configure, when you use a feature that reaches the network.
- Safety: choose an approval mode from review-every-action to full autonomy; shell commands are sandboxed where the OS supports it.

## Key capabilities

- Agentic tools: read, write, edit, patch, search files, run shell, inspect git, fetch and search the web, and drive pull requests. Pure reads run concurrently; writes and commands stay sequential.
- Structural code search with a bundled ripgrep and ast-grep (syntax-tree matching).
- See its own localhost: start a dev server, screenshot the page, read the console, and iterate. A live preview panel docks beside the chat.
- Subagents and adversarial multi-agent review of your diff for correctness, security, and quality.
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers over stdio, HTTP, or SSE; custom read-only agents and on-demand skills defined in Markdown.

## Platforms

- macOS 12 Monterey or newer (Apple Silicon and Intel)
- Windows 10 or newer (x64)
- Linux x64 (glibc 2.35+, e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+)
- Standalone terminal CLI on any platform with Node 22+
